catalog_quote: Ударение динамическое (силовое). ... Ударение может падать на любой слог словоформы (но не на энклитики): 1-й: vàzdel ʽподнимаетʼ pàrpale ʽназадʼ lùbenica ʽарбузʼ 2-й: anèl ʽнесётʼ paplòno ʽодеялоʼ kumpànija ʽгруппа цыганʼ 3-й: barvalò ʽбогатыйʼ buzdugàno ʽпалицаʼ 4-й: melaxnořò ʽсмугленькийʼ ... Ударение смыслоразличительно для морфологических категорий (регулярно в ряде словоизменительных типов): mỳca ʽкошкаʼ (прямой падеж): mycà ʽкошкуʼ (косвенный падеж) [p. 60] ... С типологической точки зрения кэлдэрарскую акцентную систему можно назвать категориальной. Это значит, что ударение слов однозначно определяется их морфологическим типом (категорией). [p. 91] ... В прямых формах: I пласт — ударение на окончании или (при нулевом окончании) на последнем слоге основы: tirv|ò, мн. tirv|è ʽкрёстный отецʼ ... řòm|, мн. řòm| ʽцыганʼ ... II пласт — ударение на одном из слогов основы: kòkal|o, мн. kòkal|a ʽкостьʼ ... paramìć|i ... harambàš| ... В косвенных формах — всегда на окончании: ед. tirv|ès, řom|ès ... [p. 92] ... В неодносложных морфемах (обычно это корни) ударен только один из слогов, причём место ударения — постоянное свойство морфемы ... Контурное правило: (1) если в слове две обязательно ударные морфемы (Ȁ), причём одна из них стоит на конце словоформы, то ударение колеблется между ними; (2) в прочих случаях ударение стоит на самой сильной морфеме справа ... На практике это означает, что ударение «стремится» вправо, насколько это возможно. [p. 94]

sweep_summary: vlax1238 (Vlax Romani) is not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title's only title hit, Glottolog ref 433498 (Moroni 2013, a German-studies book review of Volodina's corpus study of syntax and prosody in German discourse, DOI 10.1515/zrs-2013-0041), is a Glottolog mis-association: the Crossref record confirms it is about German, not Romani; it is paywalled and irrelevant (priority none). No relevant new titles came from this search of works with stress in the title. Three first-hand statements of Vlax word stress were already held by the project from our earlier reading and were re-read with page mapping verified: Oslon 2018 (Kalderash reference grammar, secs. 1.5 p. 60 and 2.7 pp. 91-92), Wagner 2012 (NW Lovari, sec. 2.4 pp. 29-31), Boretzky & Igla 1994 (pan-SE-European sketch based on Kalderash, pp. 370-371). All three agree: stress is morphologically conditioned and mobile — inherited nominals and basic verb forms are final-stressed (nominative ending / person ending), oblique case forms stress the oblique marker (case/TAM suffixes behave like clitics), loans have stem (mostly penultimate) stress, de-verbs initial; Wagner adds that many NW Lovari speakers level the pattern under Czech/Slovak contact. Best statement: Oslon 2018 sec. 2.7/2.7.1(a). Nothing to supersede (no catalog record). new files saved: and in, with updated.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No single fixed position: stress is phonologically free and assigned by morphological class and lexical stratum. Inherited (stratum I) nouns/adjectives/pronouns are stressed on the final syllable (ending, or last stem syllable if no ending); borrowed (stratum II) nominals carry lexical stem stress (typically the syllable before the thematic vowel, i.e. penult); oblique case endings always take the stress; verbs stress the person ending except d-/ajv-class and mediopassive stems; enclitics, postfixes (-a, -sas), articles and most prepositions are never stressed. Stress distinguishes morphological forms (mỳca nom. : mycà obl.).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Narrow word form has at most one stress; 'wide' word forms (compounds/proclitic combinations such as sa-da-jèk, li-oxtò) may carry two stresses, with clash-resolution rules (Oslon sec. 2.7.3, pp. 96-97). Wagner 2012: 179-180 notes weaker secondary stresses on modifying elements of compounds in Lovari.
new_statements.exceptions: A few minimal pairs (kakò 'this' : kàko 'uncle'); minor vacillation in some nom.pl. forms (talojà ~ talòja) and imperative aźukə̀r ~ aźùkər; some disyllabic prepositions stressed (inťà, katàr, karìng); negative/quantifier pronouns with non-final stress (khònik, sàko, sòřo); stress may shift in singing; in fast speech stress weakly audible.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (узкая/широкая словоформа incl. clitics); enclitics excluded from stress; examples are citation and text forms from fieldwork with audio; phrase intonation treated separately (sec. 4.8).
new_statements.identity_note: Best statement (Oslon 2018) describes the Kalderash (Kelderar, 'kotljary-moldovaja') dialect of Vlax Romani as spoken in Russia/Ukraine = Glottolog dialect kald1238 under vlax1238. Corroborating statements: Wagner 2012 for North West Lovari (Czech/Slovak Lovara) = lova1240; Boretzky & Igla 1994 sketch explicitly based on Kalderaš (with notes on Gurbet/Arli/Bugurdži, the latter two non-Vlax). All are Northern Vlax; no first-hand statement for Southern Vlax (Gurbet, Ajia Varvara) was opened.

Это значит, что ударение слов однозначно определяется их морфологическим типом (категорией). [...] (а) существительное. В прямых формах: I пласт — ударение на окончании или (при нулевом окончании) на последнем слоге основы: tirv|ò, мн. tirv|è ʽкрёстный отецʼ; ćirikl|ì, мн. ćirikľ|à ʽптицаʼ; řòm|, мн. řòm| ʽцыганʼ [...]; II пласт — ударение на одном из слогов основы: kòkal|o, мн. kòkal|a ʽкостьʼ [...]. В косвенных формах — всегда на окончании: ед. tirv|ès, řom|ès, ćirikľ|à, řus|òs [...]. Как видно, большинство существительных имеет подвижное ударение
new_statements.translation: From a typological point of view the Kalderash accent system can be called categorial. That is, the stress of a word is unambiguously determined by its morphological type (category). [...] (a) Noun. In direct forms: stratum I [inherited] — stress on the ending or (with zero ending) on the last syllable of the stem: tirvò, pl. tirvè 'godfather'; ćiriklì, pl. ćirikľà 'bird'; řòm, pl. řòm 'Rom' [...]; stratum II [loans] — stress on one of the stem syllables: kòkalo, pl. kòkala 'bone' [...]. In oblique forms — always on the ending: sg. tirvès, řomès, ćirikľà, řusòs [...]. As can be seen, most nouns have mobile stress.
new_statements.citation: Oslon, M. V. 2018. Jazyk kotljarov-moldovaja: Grammatika kelderarskogo dialekta cyganskogo jazyka v russkojazyčnom okruženii. Moskva: Izd. Dom JaSK. (Kalderash Romani, Vlax; first-hand reference grammar, sec. 2.7 'Udarenie')
new_statements.reading: Vlax (Kalderash) word stress is not fixed to a syllable position: it is morphologically/lexically conditioned and mobile. Inherited words carry the old final stress (nominative on the last syllable/ending), loans keep stem (mostly penultimate) stress, and every oblique form stresses the case ending; finite verbs stress the person ending (Boretzky & Igla 1994: 371; Wagner 2012: 29-30 concur, Wagner for Lovari). A catalog's classification would be 'lexical/morphological (unbounded), inherited default = final' rather than any fixed-position type; stress can fall on syllables 1-4 (Oslon p. 60).

new_statements.relation_note: Snippet-level only. Matras' general statement (grammatical stress: root-final in the inherited component, on Layer I endings when inflected; European loans and contact dialects deviate) matches the catalog's 'morphological' record from Oslon 2018 (categorial accent system; layer I nouns stressed on the ending or stem-final, obliques on the case ending) and the Boretzky & Igla 1994 / Wagner 2012 notes already held by the project. It adds nothing Kalderaš-specific beyond them; the sentences on p. 62 (indexed 'Kalderaš') and p. 63 (indexed 'Vlax group') remain unread, so a Kalderaš-specific refinement or contradiction cannot be excluded but none is suggested by the fragments.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Matras describes Early Romani and the 'conservative' present-day dialects as having word-level grammatical (morphologically conditioned) stress: in the inherited (pre-European, thematic) component stress falls on the last syllable of the lexical root when no grammatical affix follows, otherwise on the older Layer I inflectional endings of nouns, pronouns, possessives, adjectives (and, per another fragment, mediopassives keep stress on the root with a possible shift to stressed person markers). Shifts toward penultimate/initial stress are attributed only to dialects in contact with initial/penult-stress languages (central Europe: Sinti/Central dialects; Albanian-influenced Prizren, Arli, Bugurdži; Finnish Romani). Kalderaš/Vlax is not among the shifting dialects in any held fragment, which is consistent with it keeping the conservative pattern; the Kalderaš-specific wording indexed to p. 62 and the Vlax-group mention indexed to p. 63 were not readable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: nothing on secondary stress in the reachable fragments
new_statements.exceptions: Fragments mention: Layer II (scanned 'Layer 11') case endings do not take the stress in conservative dialects ('grammatical stress in Layer 1 endings that precede Layer 11 endings, thus exempting forms like roméskero ‘of the man’ from the shift'); demonstratives with penultimate stress in attributive position but final stress elsewhere (Welsh Romani sentence, p. 63-64); vowel length 'independent of stress'. None of these is stated for Kalderaš specifically in what was readable.
new_statements.identity_note: Matras 2002 is a pan-Romani introduction; its index treats Kalderaš (Kelderaš) as a Northern Vlax dialect with page references 50, 53, 57, 61, 62, 65 in ch. 4 and 'Vlax group' at 63; the catalog record for vlax1238 rests on Oslon 2018 (Kalderash of Russian-speaking surroundings, kotljary-moldovaja). The reachable Matras fragments speak of Early Romani / conservative dialects generally, not of Kalderaš by name.

tone_statements.citation: Arvaniti, Amalia. 2016. Analytical Decisions in Intonation Research and the Role of Representations: Lessons from Romani. Laboratory Phonology: Journal of the Association for Laboratory Phonology 7(1): 6, pp. 1-43.
tone_statements.quote: Evidence from questions and narrow focus utterances makes it clear that pitch rises in Romani are not an exponent of stress or a lexical property of words, but an independent phenomenon. … Utterances like these clearly show that typologically Thrace Romani is a linguistic variety which has stress and uses pitch primarily to encode intonational di erences. … The above discussion of stress indicates that pitch modulation in Romani should be treated as postlexical, i.e., as intonation.
tone_statements.locator: Art. 6 pp. 13-14 of 43, end of sec. 4.1 'Stress' and opening of sec. 4.2 'Tonal inventory'; restated sec. 5.3 p. 29: 'Romani would be classed as a language that uses only postlexical tones (intonation) in combination with stress.'
tone_statements.summary: Greek Thrace Vlax Romani has no lexical tone or lexical pitch accent: pitch is postlexical intonation (H*, L* accents, edge tones) on top of word stress, shown with F0 tracks from a fieldwork corpus.

tone_statements.citation: Adamou, Evangelia & Amalia Arvaniti. 2010. Language-specific and universal patterns in narrow focus marking in Romani. In Speech Prosody 2010 (Fifth International Conference on Speech Prosody, Chicago), paper 086, 1-4. ISCA.
tone_statements.quote: Our data show that in Komotini Romani pitch modulation is a phrasal property that is, intonation. Pitch is used to mark prosodic boundaries, indicate the pragmatic function of an utterance and highlight particular words in discourse. … in each one some pitch movements co-occur with stressed syllables and others with phrasal boundaries. We analyze the former as pitch accents and the latter as boundary tones … However, unlike French, Romani has lexical stress
tone_statements.locator: p. 2, sec. 3.1 'Intonation and the marking of broad focus'; last clause p. 3, end of sec. 3.2
tone_statements.summary: No lexical tone: pitch is purely intonational (pitch accents on stressed syllables, boundary tones at phrase edges). Lexical stress, mostly final in native words, shifts leftward to mark focus.

sources.citation: Wagner, Peter. 2012. A Grammar of North West Lovari Romani. PhD thesis, Charles University, Prague. Lovari Romani (lova1240), a Vlax dialect spoken in Czech/Slovak contact.
sources.quote: pp. 29-30: "1. In nominals belonging to oikoclitic classes and in nominatives and in present tense-subjunctive or perfect tense forms of verbs of the e-, uv- and in-conjugation, stress is placed on the last syllable, be it a stem syllable or a suffix. This is a retention of the original, post-Indian stress pattern: šá'vo “young Rom, Rom guy”, rom'ňi “Rom woman”, á'nav “name”, man'gel “ask”, zurá'lo “strong” [...]; 2. Oblique nominals and verbs in other forms keep stress on the oblique and on the verb form from (1.), on which they are based, with case and TAM markers added like clitics after the upset of early Romani stress: šá'veske, rom'ňan, ána'vestar, man'gelas [...]; 3. Verbs of the de-conjugation are stressed on the first syllable [...]; 4. Xenoclitic nominals show unpredictable behaviour governed by lexicon"
sources.note: Sec. 2.4 Word Stress (pp. 29-31): stress fixed by rules that depend on many factors incl. lexicon; independent of vowel length; rule 1: oikoclitic nominals and present/subjunctive/perfect verb forms stress the last syllable (retention of post-Indian pattern: šá'vo, rom'ňi, man'gel); obliques/TAM markers added like clitics keep that stress; de-verbs initial; xenoclitic nouns lexical, prefer penult, Czech/Slovak loans initial; adnominal stress weak/initial; clitic copula and pronouns do not affect stress; compounds show weaker secondary stresses on modifiers (p. 179-180).

Grammatik, sec. 1.4 'Akzentuierung' (sketch based on Kalderash, with Gurbet/Arli/Bugurdži/Prizren contrasts). Rosetta Project scan of pp. 367-372.
sources.quote: p. 370 (scanned, umlauts restored): "Es gibt einen konservativen Akzentuierungstyp, der sich am besten im Kald., einigermaßen gut im südlichen Gurbet und in Varianten des Arli und sehr schlecht im Bug. erkennen läßt. [...] 1.4.1. Nomina. Ererbte Nomina auf -o, -i und Kons. betonen im Nom.Sg. die Endsilbe, ebenso im Pl. -e, -ja, in den übrigen Kasus den Obliquusmarker -es-, -a-, -en- [...]. Entlehnte Nomina betonen im Nom. die Silbe vor dem vokalischen Auslaut -o, -i, -a u.a., seltener eine Silbe davor; in den Obliqui ist aber ebenfalls der Obliquusmarker [...] betont." p. 371: "1.4.2. Verben. Das finite Verb betont die Personalendung im engeren Sinne, also im Präs., Futur und Ipf. -av-, -es-, -el- usw., im Prät. und Plqu. -om-, -an-, -a(s)- usw. Eine Ausnahme macht das Präs. der auf -d auslautenden Verben, das die Silbe vor der Personalendung betont; vgl. phurd-el."
sources.locator: pp. 370-371 (scan pp. 4-5), secs. 1.4.1 Nomina and 1.4.2 Verben
sources.note: Conservative accent type best preserved in Kalderaš: inherited nouns in -o, -i, C stress the final syllable in Nom.Sg. and Pl., oblique marker in other cases; vocative -a unstressed; borrowed nouns stress the syllable before the final vowel; finite verbs stress the person ending, except d-verbs (phúrd-el); passive present penult. Outside Kalderaš word stress often fluctuates with sentence rhythm.

sources.citation: Arvaniti, Amalia. 2016. Analytical Decisions in Intonation Research and the Role of Representations: Lessons from Romani. Laboratory Phonology: Journal of the Association for Laboratory Phonology 7(1): 6, pp. 1-43.
sources.quote: Evidence from questions and narrow focus utterances makes it clear that pitch rises in Romani are not an exponent of stress or a lexical property of words, but an independent phenomenon. … Utterances like these clearly show that typologically Thrace Romani is a linguistic variety which has stress and uses pitch primarily to encode intonational di erences. … The above discussion of stress indicates that pitch modulation in Romani should be treated as postlexical, i.e., as intonation.
sources.locator: Art. 6 pp. 13-14 of 43, end of sec. 4.1 'Stress' and opening of sec. 4.2 'Tonal inventory'; restated sec. 5.3 p. 29: 'Romani would be classed as a language that uses only postlexical tones (intonation) in combination with stress.'
sources.note: Describes another variety. Greek Thrace Vlax Romani has no lexical tone or lexical pitch accent: pitch is postlexical intonation (H*, L* accents, edge tones) on top of word stress, shown with F0 tracks from a fieldwork corpus.

sources.citation: Adamou, Evangelia & Amalia Arvaniti. 2010. Language-specific and universal patterns in narrow focus marking in Romani. In Speech Prosody 2010 (Fifth International Conference on Speech Prosody, Chicago), paper 086, 1-4. ISCA.
sources.quote: Our data show that in Komotini Romani pitch modulation is a phrasal property that is, intonation. Pitch is used to mark prosodic boundaries, indicate the pragmatic function of an utterance and highlight particular words in discourse. … in each one some pitch movements co-occur with stressed syllables and others with phrasal boundaries. We analyze the former as pitch accents and the latter as boundary tones … However, unlike French, Romani has lexical stress
sources.locator: p. 2, sec. 3.1 'Intonation and the marking of broad focus'; last clause p. 3, end of sec. 3.2
sources.note: No lexical tone: pitch is purely intonational (pitch accents on stressed syllables, boundary tones at phrase edges). Lexical stress, mostly final in native words, shifts leftward to mark focus.
sources.venue: Speech Prosody 2010 (Fifth International Conference on Speech Prosody, Chicago), paper 086

sources.citation: Arvaniti, Amalia & Evangelia Adamou. 2011. Focus Expression in Romani. In Mary Byram Washburn et al. (eds.), Proceedings of the 28th West Coast Conference on Formal Linguistics (WCCFL 28), 240-248. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.
sources.note: States that Komotini Romani has lexical (word) stress, final in native vocabulary and penult/antepenult in loans and with certain suffixes/enclitics, and that pitch modulation is NOT lexically determined but phrasal: an autosegmental-metrical intonation sketch with at least three post-lexical pitch accents (L+H* ~ H*, H+L*, L*) and H%/L% boundary tones; content words typically accented; narrow focus marked by accentuation plus a stress-shift to an earlier syllable. I.e. a stress language with intonational, not lexical, tones.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 28th West Coast Conference on Formal Linguistics (WCCFL 28)

tone.quote: Similarly to other conservative Romani dialects (Matras 2002), Komotini Romani has final stress in the native parts of its vocabulary. [...] Our data show that in Komotini Romani pitch modulation is not lexically determined but is a phrasal property. Thus, pitch is used to mark prosodic boundaries, indicate the pragmatic function of utterances and highlight particular words in discourse. [...] We tentatively recognize at least three types of pitch accent in the Komotini Romani system, L+H* (possibly a simple H*), H+L* and L* and at least one level of phrasing that is delimited by the presence of a H% or L% boundary tone.
